- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect potential rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-7 days; apply downward correction of 1-2% to avoid overreaction.
- If 3+ consecutive days of low sentiment (0.00 or negative) precede forecast, model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to account for lagged recovery.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-cycle momentum; if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% in final 7–10 days.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from 30d forecast (e.g., >3% error in last 5 days), check sentiment for reversal signals — if sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven correction.
